note: Territory index. To add a nation: add its data file under public/data/web/territories/ and one entry here. No code change needed. Colors: Okabe-Ito colorblind-safe palette, one per nation.

nations.name: Chickasaw
nations.note: Extent shown is the 1786 Treaty of Hopewell frame; its southern edge is not fixed by the sources.
nations.mapNote: General area (1786 Hopewell frame): approximate, not a boundary.

nations.name: Cherokee
nations.mapNote: General area: the 1771 Donelson cession and the 1770 Lochaber wedge (hatched, full documented shapes, including the parts outside Kentucky) and the Chickamauga counties. Approximate, low-medium confidence, not a boundary.
nations.note: Main-map shape = sourced treaty/survey shapes (1770 wedge, 1771 survey area) drawn in full, solid lines inside Kentucky and the Chickamauga county footprint. Pre-1768 Kentucky use has no dated boundary and is not drawn.

nations.name: Shawnee
nations.mapNote: Presence in Kentucky c.1735–c.1782; claim to most of Kentucky asserted by 1768 (whole-state outline = most generous estimate, not a boundary). Ohio town counties and the 1774 Ohio River line run to 1795. Approximate, low-medium confidence.
nations.note: Main-map shape = claim area (Kentucky outline, most generous estimate of “most of Kentucky”; not a boundary), the 1774 Ohio River line and the Ohio town counties. No boundary is sourced.

nations.name: Six Nations (Haudenosaunee)
nations.mapNote: Approximate general area of the Haudenosaunee homeland in New York and Pennsylvania (tint), and, hatched, the Kentucky east of the Tennessee River sold to the Crown in 1768 (a cession claim, not where people lived). Low-medium confidence, not a boundary.
nations.note: Kentucky east of the Tennessee River was sold to the Crown at Fort Stanwix 1768 on a Six Nations conquest claim that the Cherokee and Shawnee disputed. The tint in New York and Pennsylvania is a general area of the homeland, built from whole counties.

nations.name: Mingo
nations.mapNote: Approximate general area of Mingo presence on the upper Ohio, 1770–1776 (whole counties, not a boundary), with three approximate points. Kentucky camp sites unknown, not drawn. Low confidence.
nations.note: Presence: an approximate general area on the upper Ohio, sourced points and a raid site; no Kentucky camp areas are known or drawn.

nations.name: Wyandot
nations.mapNote: Approximate general area of Wyandot towns on the Sandusky River and near Detroit, c.1745–1795 (whole counties, not a boundary); Kentucky only as 1780 and 1782 raid sites. The 1785 Fort McIntosh allotment is hatched as a county approximation. Low–medium confidence.
nations.note: A general area in Ohio and Michigan, sourced town and raid points; no Kentucky camp areas are known or drawn.

nations.name: Delaware (Lenape)
nations.mapNote: Approximate general area of the Delaware (Lenape) Ohio towns c.1750–1795 (Muskingum and Tuscarawas valleys) and the ten-county 1804 Indiana cession (whole counties, not a boundary), plus Bird’s 1780 route in Kentucky. Kentucky camp sites unknown, not drawn.
nations.note: Ohio and Indiana: a general area of the towns, the 1780 route inside Kentucky, the 1785 allotment and the 1804 cession. No Kentucky camp areas are drawn.

nations.name: Miami (with Wea and Piankashaw)
nations.mapNote: Approximate general area of the Wabash country (Miami, Wea, Piankashaw) c.1750–1805, from Fort Wayne to Vincennes (whole counties, not a boundary), with the ten-county 1804 cession. Northern Kentucky hunting ground: no area drawn.
nations.note: Wabash valley in Indiana: a general area of the towns and the 1804 cession; Kentucky hunting is described in text only.

nations.name: Kickapoo (with Mascouten)
nations.mapNote: Approximate general area in Indiana and Illinois, c.1740–1819 (the Wabash and Vermilion country, whole counties, not a boundary). The Mascouten have no area of their own and are shown here. No Kentucky villages are documented. Low confidence.
nations.note: A general area in Indiana and Illinois; no Kentucky villages are documented.

nations.name: Illinois Confederation (Kaskaskia, Cahokia)
nations.mapNote: Approximate general area of the Illinois towns on the Mississippi (1778) and of the claim declared in 1803 (southern Illinois, whole counties, not a boundary; the inland edge is unlocated). Low–medium confidence.
nations.note: Two town points and a general area of the 1803 declared claim in Illinois; the inland calls are unlocated, so the edge is a rough guess.

nations.name: Potawatomi
nations.mapNote: Approximate general area of Potawatomi presence, c.1640–1809: Green Bay and Door County, then southern Michigan, northern Indiana and northeast Illinois (whole counties, not a boundary). Low confidence.
nations.note: A general area in Wisconsin, Michigan, Indiana and Illinois; Detroit and Chicago points; no Kentucky presence.

nations.name: Ojibwe (Chippewa) and Odawa
nations.mapNote: Approximate general area of Odawa and Ojibwe presence around Detroit, Saginaw and the Maumee, c.1700–1780 (whole counties, not a boundary), and Bird’s 1780 route, solid in Kentucky. The wider homeland to the north is not drawn. Low confidence. The Odawa story about Egushawa is separate.
nations.note: A general area in Michigan and Ohio, and Bird’s June 1780 war road in Kentucky; the wider homeland is not drawn.
